# Polyworld Fast XP

> Run a Gota match synchronously and download its replay and your bot's logs.

## Make a request

Send **POST `/v1/games/gota/run`** on this server, with:

- `Content-Type: application/json`
- `Authorization: Bearer <fast-xp-token>`

Use the fast-XP service's shared caller token, supplied by its operator. An
Observatory user token is not the caller token for this server.

The JSON body contains a seed and a roster of bots. Supply your own bot's BASIC
source text inline. Select submitted opponents using policy-version UUIDs or
exact policy labels such as `my-bot:v12`. The server fetches submitted policies
using its own Observatory credential; callers do not need their source.

```json
{
  "seed": 743478993,
  "roster": [
    {"slot": 0, "player": {"source": "print selfId\nend"}},
    {"player": {"policy_ref": "109b99c1-3bb7-4276-b17e-378b43a97874"}}
  ],
  "config": {"max_ticks": 28800}
}
```

This puts your source in seat 0 and fills seats 1–9 with the referenced bot
(Richard's benchmark policy). Replace the short printing script with your full
BASIC bot. To send a local file without hand-escaping its contents:

```sh
# FAST_XP_URL is this server's origin; FAST_XP_TOKEN is its caller token.
jq -n --rawfile source ./my-bot.bas \
  '{seed:743478993, roster:[
    {slot:0, player:{source:$source}},
    {player:{policy_ref:"109b99c1-3bb7-4276-b17e-378b43a97874"}}
  ], config:{max_ticks:28800}}' > request.json
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 180 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FAST_XP_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json "$FAST_XP_URL/v1/games/gota/run" -o result.zip
```

Only unpack `result.zip` after a successful HTTP response; errors are JSON.

## Roster and settings

- Gota has ten seats, numbered 0–9. Seats 0–4 are Red; 5–9 are Blue.
- Every `player` must contain exactly one of `source` or `policy_ref`.
- `slot: 0` through `slot: 9` pins an entry to that seat. Pinned seats must be unique.
- Omit `slot` (or use `-1`) to provide a bot for unfilled seats. The server fills
  seats in ascending order, cycling through these unpinned entries in roster
  order. Pinned entries are not reused. With your bot pinned to 0 and three
  unpinned opponents A/B/C, seats 1–9 become A/B/C/A/B/C/A/B/C.
- To fill every seat with your own bot, use one unpinned `source` entry. If all
  entries are pinned, supply all ten seats.
- `source`: BASIC source text, up to 64 KiB per bot.
- `policy_ref`: a submitted policy version. The server downloads and runs its
  uploaded artifact, up to 16 MiB.
- `seed` is required: a signed 32-bit integer.
- `config` is optional. `config.max_ticks` defaults to 28800; valid values are
  1–28800. This bounds battle ticks, plus drafting. It is not wall-clock seconds.
- Supply actual source text, not a local path or URL. `random`, `top_n`, batch
  targets and unknown fields are not supported. Resolve leaderboard opponents
  to policy references before submitting.

## Response and timing

The connection stays open while the game runs. A successful response is HTTP
200 with `Content-Type: application/zip`, containing:

- `replay.replay`
- `logs/slot-N.txt` for each seat using inline `source`

There are no source files or logs for `policy_ref` seats in the response, even
if you own that submitted policy. Use inline source for any seat whose logs you
need. There is no job ID or polling endpoint.

`Server-Timing` reports `run`, `fetch`, `worker`, and `zip` durations in
milliseconds. Full matches can take tens of seconds. Allow enough client timeout;
the native worker's execution deadline is 120 seconds, plus fetching and transfer.

## Errors

Errors normally return JSON `{"error":"message"}`. Check HTTP status before
treating the response as a ZIP.

- 400: invalid request, unsupported fields, or invalid/ambiguous policy reference.
- 401: missing or incorrect fast-XP caller token.
- 404: unknown route or policy version.
- 409: selected policy has no downloadable player file.
- 413: JSON request exceeds 4 MiB, including inline source.
- 415: incorrect content type.
- 422: Policy loading or BASIC compilation failed. Only inline-source diagnostics are disclosed.
- 502: policy lookup/download/verification failed; policy artifacts may be
  at most 16 MiB. Read the error message for the failing stage.
- 503: capacity is full or the server lacks its Observatory credential. For
  capacity errors, wait for `Retry-After` before retrying; configuration errors
  need the operator to fix the server.
- 504: a policy fetch or game execution timed out.
- 500: game worker failed; the operator can inspect server diagnostics.

GET `/healthz` returns `ok`. This document is sufficient to make a request;
[run.md](run.md) contains additional reference details.
